svg.text: Dash computer: Pi 5, screen, cameras, USB, audio
Teryx OS wiring, sheet 'dash'. Made from config/wiring.yaml by `python -m teryx wiring`. Don't edit this file.
Labels: wire id, size, fuse (if the wire has its own), and anything in between. Faded = optional. Hover for notes. Full table: docs/wiring/README.md

g.title: X01: PI5.HDMI0 -> SCREEN.HDMI
X02: SCREEN.USB -> PI5.USB2_B - Touch. Screen only does touch over USB. Right-angle lead, cable-tied to the box
X03: CAM_REAR.VID -> TCAM_DONGLE.VID_R - Shielded video lead, soldered
X05: RELAYS.NO7 -> CAM_REAR.V12 - 2 A inline fuse. On with the key, like the trailer camera
X03b: CAM_REAR.VID_GND -> TCAM_DONGLE.VID_R_GND
X04: TCAM_DONGLE.CSI -> PI5.CSI1 - Camera ribbon, 2nd port
X07: CARPLAY.USB -> PI5.USB2_A - CarPlay dongle is USB only. Right-angle lead, dongle zip-tied down inside the box
X11: CAM_FRONT.CSI -> PI5.CSI0
X13: AIHAT.PCIE -> PI5.PCIE - Keep the PCIe port free for this
X14: AIHAT.HDR -> PI5.HAT_HDR - 16 mm stacking header over the Active Cooler
X15: PI5.P1_3V3 -> PI_CAN.VCC
X16: PI5.P23_SCLK -> PI_CAN.SCK
X17: PI5.P19_MOSI -> PI_CAN.SI
X18: PI_CAN.SO -> PI5.P21_MISO
X19: PI5.P24_CE0 -> PI_CAN.CS
X20: PI_CAN.INT -> PI5.P22_GPIO25
X21: DAC_HAT.OUT -> AMP.IN - RCA to RCA lead out through the Pi box's spare PG7 gland
X32: PI5.P8_TXD -> MODEM_4G.R - Soldered lead, 115200 baud
X33: MODEM_4G.T -> PI5.P10_RXD - Soldered lead. Measure T first: 3.3 V ok, else BSS138
X25: PI5.P12_GPIO18 -> DAC_HAT.BCK - jumper lead
X26: PI5.P35_GPIO19 -> DAC_HAT.LRCK - jumper lead
X27: PI5.P40_GPIO21 -> DAC_HAT.DIN - jumper lead
X28: PI5.P3_SDA -> DAC_HAT.SDA - jumper lead
X29: PI5.P5_SCL -> DAC_HAT.SCL - jumper lead
X30: PI5.P2_5V -> DAC_HAT.V5 - jumper lead
X31: DAC_HAT.GND -> PI5.GND - jumper lead
X22: AMP.SPK -> SPEAKERS.IN
X34: AMP.SUB -> SUB.IN - Amp ch 3 + 4 bridged (ch 3 + and ch 4 -, check the amp's label)
X23: PI5.P3_SDA -> IMU.SDA
X35: PI5.P17_3V3 -> IMU.VCC
X36: IMU.GND -> PI5.GND
X24: PI5.P5_SCL -> IMU.SCL
PI5: Raspberry Pi 5 8GB - The 40-pin header and the PCIe port are kept for the AI HAT+ 2. CAN module wires go to header pins that come up through the HAT
g.text: HAT_HDR 40-pin header to the 16 mm sta…

g.title: SCREEN: 10.1 in touch screen - 1280x800, HDMI + USB touch, 3.5 mm audio in
CARPLAY: Carlinkit CPC200-CCPA
CAM_FRONT: Camera Module 3 Wide (front) - Inside the screen housing, 200-300 mm ribbon

TCAM_DONGLE: Analogue video to camera-ribbon (CSI) board, ADV7280-M (rear + trailer) - No USB (Sam). The cameras run in CVBS (PAL) mode into this board, which sits in the Pi box on the Pi's 2nd camera ribbon port. ADV7280-M has several analogue inputs picked in software (adv728x-m overlay, adv7180 driver), so it swaps rear/trailer itself, no relay. A spare input can take a small cabin camera later. Pi 5 support for these boards is not proven yet: bench test it first
AIHAT: AI HAT+ 2 (later) - Not buying yet. Room, cooling (about 4.5 W) and the PCIe port stay free for it
IMU: IMU (roll / pitch)

DAC_HAT: Raspberry Pi DAC+ (on jumper leads) - PCM5122 DAC HAT (ex IQaudio DAC+), RCA line out to the amp. Sits on standoffs in the right-hand end of the Pi box, off the Pi, so the top of the Pi stays free for the AI HAT+ 2. Joined by 7 male-to-female jumper leads (about 20 cm), not a full 40-way ribbon: a ribbon would cover the header pins the CAN board, 4G board and IMU leads plug onto. Uses GPIO 18, 19, 21 (I2S), 2 and 3 (I2C, shared with the IMU: DAC 0x4D, IMU 0x68), 5 V and GND. Nothing else on the Pi uses 18-21 (CAN is SPI0 + GPIO 25, 4G is UART GPIO 14/15). The ID EEPROM pins 27/28 are left off, so it never fights the AI HAT's EEPROM; set the overlay by hand: scripts/audio-setup.sh --i2s iqaudio-dacplus. A dab of hot glue on the leads at both ends against vibration. Later the leads move onto the AI HAT's stacking header pins

MODEM_4G: SIMCom A7670SA 4G board - 6-pin header S G V K T R G. V takes 5-10 V from the spare Mini560 5 V buck. NEVER raw 12 V (10 V max, and the car runs 14.4 V with spikes). K is tied to ground on the board, so it starts by itself. T/R are 115200 baud TTL to the Pi's GPIO 15/14; measure T before connecting (3.3 V ok, else BSS138). Micro USB also on board. Its GNSS (FASE version, u.FL GPS socket on Sam's board) is the dash GPS too, so there is no separate USB GPS. Check on arrival that it gets a fix with the SIM out / 4G off. No USB: it's on the header pins (soldered leads), so texts, GPS and slow data only, no live video over 4G
PI_CAN: MCP2515 CAN module (Pi) - Seeed MCP2515 + SN65HVD230 on the Pi box wall

CAM_REAR: Rear camera (200 degree, Sam's) - Sam thinks it's AHD. Set to CVBS/PAL mode, soldered shielded video lead to the analogue-to-ribbon board. Rear or trailer is picked in software when the trailer plug is in. 12 V from the accessory relay (relay 7) through its own 2 A inline fuse

AMP: 4-ch class D amp (AliExpress, 4 x 63 W RMS at 4 ohm) - Sam's pick. 4 x 63 W RMS at 4 ohm, or 2 x 200 W RMS bridged at 4 ohm; built-in 90 Hz high and low pass; 8-16 V; up to 33 A flat out (16.5 A on music); 145 x 100 x 45 mm. Channels 1 and 2 drive the Kenwoods (set the HPF on). Channels 3 and 4 bridged (200 W at 4 ohm) drive the Kicker KM104 sub (LPF on, gain set so it stays under the sub's 150 W RMS)

SPEAKERS: Kenwood KFC-2053MRB 8 in marine speakers (pair) - Sam has these. 8 in 2-way, 4 ohm, about 50 W RMS each (100 W the pair), 180 mm cut-out, about 86 mm mounting depth (Kenwood spec page). One amp channel each; speaker cable 1.5 mm² is plenty. In sealed printed pods on the roll cage (cad/parts/speaker_pod.scad, docs/speaker-pods.md); the cable goes in through a PG7 gland underneath each pod

SUB: Kicker KM104 10 in marine subwoofer - Sam has bought it (18 Nov). 10 in, 4 ohm, 150 W RMS, 30-500 Hz. On amp ch 3 + 4 bridged, low pass on (90 Hz, matches the pods' EQ handover). Sealed printed box under the seat, on hold until Sam scans the space. 1.5 mm² speaker cable

RELAYS: 16-ch relay board, channels 1-8 - One 16-channel board of mechanical 5 V relays with opto and JD-VCC jumper (AliExpress cart), in an aux box next to the control box. RELAYS2 is channels 9-16 of the same board. The solid state G3MB-202P board Sam has is AC only and won't turn off on 12 V DC. JD-VCC jumper off, coils on 5 V, inputs from 3.3 V
